# Audit instructions

This workspace holds one pull request against the Loa framework repository, frozen for evaluation.

- `PR.md` — the PR title and description
- `head.diff` — the complete change (unified diff, base → head)
- `base/` — every touched file before the change
- `head/` — every touched file after the change

Audit the change as the security auditor for this repository. There is no sprint plan, beads database, implementation report or `grimoires/loa/a2a/` directory here — the PR files above are the entire input; skip any pre-flight step that needs them and do not ask questions.

Write your audit to `audit.md` in this directory using the Write tool. Cite every finding as `head/<path>:<line>` with line numbers taken from the `head/` files. Follow your auditor skill's output format and end the file with its machine-readable verdict trailer.
----
# Task brief

## Criterion

review the pull request, report each defect it introduces with the file and line it sits on, and give a merge verdict

## Task

# Task: review a pull request

The directory `pr/` holds one pull request against a repository of shell scripts, tests and documentation, frozen for evaluation. The change: sprint-252 decision surfaces, part 1 — interview rounds, fact/decision attribution, the decision ledger, operator-only commands.

The pull request is laid out as:

- `pr/PR.md` — the title and description
- `pr/head.diff` — the complete change (unified diff, base to head)
- `pr/base/` — every touched file before the change
- `pr/head/` — every touched file after the change

Review the change as the senior technical reviewer for the repository: find the defects it introduces and decide whether it can merge. Do not change any file under `pr/`.

## Output contract

Write your review to `review.md` at the repository root (a review workflow that also writes its own report files may do so; `review.md` follows this shape regardless):

- one finding per line, in the form `head/<path>:<line> — <description>`, where `<path>` is the file's path under `pr/head/` and `<line>` is a line number in that file;
- a final line that is exactly `Verdict: APPROVED` or `Verdict: CHANGES_REQUIRED`.
----
head/.claude/scripts/lib/dec-write-lib.sh:184 — CRITICAL: `live_run_signal` is `ctx_signals | grep -q` under pipefail; with two or more live signals (fresh unattended marker + RUNNING run state) the producer dies of SIGPIPE, the pipeline returns 141 and the confirm refusal at line 509 never fires (reproduced 5/5: rows moved to decided during a live run).
head/.claude/scripts/lib/dec-write-lib.sh:183 — HIGH: `is_unattended` counts the PRD `**Status:**` line (lines 177-180) as an unattended signal, so with an autonomous PRD the operator's confirm drops its --answer-ref (line 314) and records decided_by agent (line 538), the operator's reject of a decided row dies (line 575), and the operator's supersede takes the agent path (lines 600-611).
head/.claude/scripts/lib/dec-write-lib.sh:251 — HIGH: any `--file` target is classed fixture before the CI/hook check at line 261, so `CI=1 … new --file grimoires/loa/decisions.yaml` writes the live ledger (reproduced), a hook or worktree can write the main ledger by path, and confirm/supersede on a --file pending path escape the refusals at lines 512 and 593.
head/.claude/scripts/lib/dec-write-lib.sh:580 — HIGH: `op_reject` rewrites only the rejected row; rejecting a proposed replacement leaves the predecessor's supersede_proposed_by stale, so every later agent supersede dies at line 601 and the operator's reject of the predecessor aborts in verify_and_swap (reproduced).
head/.claude/scripts/lib/dec-write-lib.sh:647 — HIGH: `import` swaps the live ledger before the --rewrite loop (mktemp/mv under set -e, lines 651-653) and before `rm -f -- "$from"` at line 655; a rewrite failure leaves the pending file in place and a retry appends the same rows under new DEC ids.
head/.claude/scripts/lib/dec-write-lib.sh:628 — HIGH: `import` locks only the live ledger; the pending file is read at line 629 and deleted at line 655 with no lock on it, so a concurrent worktree writer's PEND row appended in between is silently lost.
head/.claude/scripts/validate-artifact.sh:550 — HIGH: the no-`--base-file` path compares against the merge-base copy but applies single-write rules (line 671 "more than one transition appended in one write"; line 682 compares fields against the last transition only), so a row that went open → proposed → decided on one branch fails validation (reproduced: 4 violations).
head/.claude/scripts/lib/dec-write-lib.sh:649 — MEDIUM: `import --rewrite` paths are unvalidated: no `..` check, no project containment, symlinks replaced by regular files (reproduced through a symlink to /tmp), unlike artifact_path at lines 289-305.
head/.claude/scripts/lib/dec-write-lib.sh:359 — MEDIUM: the operator-only gate is the caller-supplied string `--recorded-by decisions-command`; any Bash session can self-confirm with decided_by operator, while the header (line 17) and decisions.md:24 state the gate as a hard property.
head/tests/unit/user-invoked-harness.bats:134 — MEDIUM: the unit suite runs a live, paid `claude -p` call (up to 180 s, line 151) whenever the CLI is on PATH and LOA_HARNESS_CHECK is unset.
head/.claude/settings.json:509 — MEDIUM: the new SessionStart hook is registered but `.claude/loa/reference/hooks-reference.md`, `scripts-reference.md`, PROCESS.md (cited by README.md:125 and AGENTS.md:32 for the full command list) and the CHANGELOG are not updated for the hook, the writer or /decisions.
head/.claude/scripts/validate-artifact.sh:526 — MEDIUM: `validate_decisions` is a ~190-line function wrapping a ~150-line jq program; move the jq to a `.jq` file loaded with `jq -f`.
head/.loa.config.yaml.example:140 — MEDIUM: the example hard-sets `pacing: rounds`, so a user who sets `interview.mode: minimal` gets rounds instead of the documented batch default (comment at line 127).
head/.claude/scripts/lib/dec-write-lib.sh:264 — LOW: the pending-file bootstrap (`cat > "$TARGET"`) runs before acquire_lock at line 468; two concurrent first writers in one worktree can truncate each other (microsecond window).
head/.claude/hooks/session-start/loa-decisions-surface.sh:69 — LOW: the jq class carries literal, invisible U+2028/U+2029 bytes instead of `  ` escapes as grimoire-index.sh:189 uses.
head/.claude/scripts/grimoire-index.sh:189 — LOW: the decisions summary is not angle-bracket-neutralised before landing in agent-read INDEX.md, unlike the session-start surface.
head/.claude/scripts/lib/dec-write-lib.sh:739 — LOW: `--help` prints line 45 (`export LC_ALL=C`) as its last line; `sed -n '2,44p'`.
head/.claude/scripts/grimoire-index.sh:217 — LOW: the catalog header still lists "observation" (removed cycle-121) and omits the new decisions family.
head/.gitignore:150 — LOW: ignore-then-negate pair for decisions.yaml (line 149 then 150) plus a new tolerance helper in validate-gitignore-state.sh:71-76; deleting the ignore line is simpler.
head/tools/check-round-independence.sh:52 — LOW: `--min-average 02` passes the regex but fails `--argjson` at line 82 with a raw jq error instead of the script's usage message.
Verdict: CHANGES_REQUIRED
----

---
name: "audit-sprint"
version: "1.1.0"
description: |
  Security and quality audit of sprint implementation.
  Final gate before sprint completion. Creates COMPLETED marker on approval.
  Resolves local sprint IDs to global IDs via Sprint Ledger.

arguments:
  - name: "sprint_id"
    type: "string"
    pattern: "^sprint-[0-9]+$"
    required: true
    description: "Sprint to audit (e.g., sprint-1)"
    examples: ["sprint-1", "sprint-2", "sprint-10"]

agent: "auditing-security"
agent_path: "skills/auditing-security/"

context_files:
  - path: "grimoires/loa/prd.md"
    required: true
    purpose: "Product requirements for context"
  - path: "grimoires/loa/sdd.md"
    required: true
    purpose: "Architecture decisions for alignment"
  - path: "grimoires/loa/sprint.md"
    required: true
    purpose: "Sprint tasks and acceptance criteria"
  - path: "grimoires/loa/ledger.json"
    required: false
    purpose: "Sprint Ledger for ID resolution"
  - path: "grimoires/loa/a2a/$ARGUMENTS.sprint_id/reviewer.md"
    required: true
    purpose: "Engineer's implementation report"
  - path: "grimoires/loa/a2a/$ARGUMENTS.sprint_id/engineer-feedback.md"
    required: true
    purpose: "Senior lead approval verification"

pre_flight:
  - check: "pattern_match"
    value: "$ARGUMENTS.sprint_id"
    pattern: "^sprint-[0-9]+$"
    error: "Invalid sprint ID. Expected format: sprint-N (e.g., sprint-1)"

  - check: "script"
    script: ".claude/scripts/validate-sprint-id.sh"
    args: ["$ARGUMENTS.sprint_id"]
    store_result: "sprint_resolution"
    purpose: "Resolve local sprint ID to global ID via ledger"

  - check: "directory_exists"
    path: "grimoires/loa/a2a/$RESOLVED_SPRINT_ID"
    error: "Sprint directory not found. Run /implement $ARGUMENTS.sprint_id first."

  - check: "file_exists"
    path: "grimoires/loa/a2a/$RESOLVED_SPRINT_ID/reviewer.md"
    error: "No implementation report found. Run /implement $ARGUMENTS.sprint_id first."

  - check: "file_exists"
    path: "grimoires/loa/a2a/$RESOLVED_SPRINT_ID/engineer-feedback.md"
    error: "Sprint has not been reviewed. Run /review-sprint $ARGUMENTS.sprint_id first."
    # Construct-aware: when a construct declares review: skip, the review gate
    # is bypassed and engineer-feedback.md won't exist. Read .run/construct-workflow.json
    # to evaluate this condition.
    skip_when:
      construct_gate: "review"
      gate_value: "skip"

  - check: "content_contains"
    path: "grimoires/loa/a2a/$RESOLVED_SPRINT_ID/engineer-feedback.md"
    pattern: "All good"
    error: "Sprint has not been approved by senior lead. Run /review-sprint $ARGUMENTS.sprint_id first."
    # Construct-aware: when a construct declares review: skip, the "All good"
    # approval check is bypassed. The construct's own workflow gates enforce quality.
    skip_when:
      construct_gate: "review"
      gate_value: "skip"

  - check: "file_not_exists"
    path: "grimoires/loa/a2a/$RESOLVED_SPRINT_ID/COMPLETED"
    error: "Sprint $ARGUMENTS.sprint_id is already COMPLETED. No audit needed."

outputs:
  - path: "grimoires/loa/a2a/$RESOLVED_SPRINT_ID/auditor-sprint-feedback.md"
    type: "file"
    description: "Audit feedback or 'APPROVED - LETS FUCKING GO'"
  - path: "grimoires/loa/a2a/$RESOLVED_SPRINT_ID/COMPLETED"
    type: "file"
    description: "Completion marker (created on approval)"
  - path: "grimoires/loa/a2a/index.md"
    type: "file"
    description: "Sprint index (status updated)"
  - path: "grimoires/loa/ledger.json"
    type: "file"
    description: "Sprint Ledger (status updated to completed)"

mode:
  default: "foreground"
  allow_background: true
---

# Audit Sprint

## Purpose

Security and quality audit of sprint implementation as the Paranoid Cypherpunk Auditor. Final gate before sprint completion. Runs AFTER senior lead approval.

## Invocation

```
/audit-sprint sprint-1
/audit-sprint sprint-1 background
```

## Agent

Launches `auditing-security` from `skills/auditing-security/`.

See: `skills/auditing-security/SKILL.md` for full workflow details.

## Prerequisites

- Sprint tasks implemented (`/implement`)
- Senior lead approved with "All good" (`/review-sprint`)
- Not already completed (no COMPLETED marker)

## Workflow

1. **Pre-flight**: Validate sprint ID, verify senior approval
2. **Context Loading**: Read PRD, SDD, sprint plan, implementation report
3. **Code Audit**: Read actual code files for security review
4. **Security Checklist**: OWASP Top 10, secrets, auth, input validation
5. **Decision**: Approve or require changes
6. **Output**: Write audit feedback or approval
7. **Completion**: Create COMPLETED marker on approval
8. **Analytics**: Update usage metrics (THJ users only)

## Arguments

| Argument | Description | Required |
|----------|-------------|----------|
| `sprint_id` | Which sprint to audit (e.g., `sprint-1`) | Yes |
| `background` | Run as subagent for parallel execution | No |

## Outputs

| Path | Description |
|------|-------------|
| `grimoires/loa/a2a/{sprint_id}/auditor-sprint-feedback.md` | Audit results |
| `grimoires/loa/a2a/{sprint_id}/COMPLETED` | Completion marker |
| `grimoires/loa/a2a/index.md` | Updated sprint status |

## Decision Outcomes

### Approval ("APPROVED - LETS FUCKING GO")

When security audit passes:
- Writes approval to `auditor-sprint-feedback.md`
- Creates `COMPLETED` marker file
- Sets sprint status to `COMPLETED`
- Next step: Move to next sprint or deployment

### Changes Required ("CHANGES_REQUIRED")

When security issues found:
- Writes detailed findings to `auditor-sprint-feedback.md`
- Includes severity (CRITICAL/HIGH/MEDIUM/LOW)
- Sets sprint status to `AUDIT_CHANGES_REQUIRED`
- Next step: `/implement sprint-N` (to fix issues)

## Security Checklist

The auditor reviews:
- **Secrets**: No hardcoded credentials, proper env vars
- **Auth/Authz**: Proper access control, no privilege escalation
- **Input Validation**: No injection vulnerabilities
- **Data Privacy**: No PII leaks, proper encryption
- **API Security**: Rate limiting, CORS, validation
- **Error Handling**: No info disclosure, proper logging
- **Code Quality**: No obvious bugs, tested error paths

## Error Handling

| Error | Cause | Resolution |
|-------|-------|------------|
| "Invalid sprint ID" | Wrong format | Use `sprint-N` format |
| "Sprint directory not found" | No A2A dir | Run `/implement` first |
| "No implementation report found" | Missing reviewer.md | Run `/implement` first |
| "Sprint has not been reviewed" | Missing engineer-feedback.md | Run `/review-sprint` first |
| "Sprint has not been approved" | No "All good" | Get senior approval first |
| "Sprint is already COMPLETED" | COMPLETED marker exists | No audit needed |

## Feedback Loop

```
/audit-sprint sprint-N
      ↓
[Security audit]
      ↓
CHANGES_REQUIRED          APPROVED
      ↓                       ↓
/implement sprint-N    [COMPLETED marker]
      ↓                       ↓
/audit-sprint sprint-N   Next sprint
```

## Sprint Ledger Integration

When a Sprint Ledger exists (`grimoires/loa/ledger.json`):

1. **ID Resolution**: Resolves `sprint-1` (local) to global ID (e.g., `3`)
2. **Directory Mapping**: Uses `a2a/sprint-3/` instead of `a2a/sprint-1/`
3. **Status Update**: Sets sprint status to `completed` in ledger on approval
4. **Consistent Paths**: All file operations use resolved global ID

### Example Resolution

```bash
# In cycle-002, sprint-1 maps to global sprint-3
/audit-sprint sprint-1
# → Resolving sprint-1 to global sprint-3
# → Reading: grimoires/loa/a2a/sprint-3/engineer-feedback.md
# → Writing: grimoires/loa/a2a/sprint-3/auditor-sprint-feedback.md
# → Creating: grimoires/loa/a2a/sprint-3/COMPLETED
# → Updating ledger: sprint-3 status = completed
```

### Legacy Mode

Without a ledger, sprint IDs are used directly (sprint-1 → a2a/sprint-1/).

## beads_rust Integration

When beads_rust is installed, the agent records security audit results:

1. **Session Start**: `br sync --import-only` to import latest state
2. **Record Audit**: `br comments add <task-id> "SECURITY AUDIT: [verdict] - [summary]"`
3. **Mark Status**: `br label add <task-id> security-approved` or `security-blocked`
4. **Session End**: `br sync --flush-only` before commit

**Protocol Reference**: See `.claude/protocols/beads-integration.md`
======
---

allowed-tools: Read, Grep, Glob, Write, Edit, WebFetch, WebSearch, Bash(.claude/scripts/verdict-derive.sh *), Bash(.claude/scripts/adversarial-review.sh *), Bash(br sync --import-only), Bash(br sync --flush-only), Bash(br comments add *), Bash(br label add *), Bash(.claude/scripts/beads/log-discovered-issue.sh *), Bash(.claude/scripts/guardrails-orchestrator.sh *), Bash(.claude/scripts/security-audit-scope.sh *), Bash(.claude/scripts/lib/profile-lib.sh knob *)

  read_files: true
  search_code: true
  write_files: true
  execute_commands:

      - command: ".claude/scripts/verdict-derive.sh"

# Paranoid Cypherpunk Auditor

<objective>
Audit code, architecture, infrastructure or sprint implementations for security and quality; produce prioritized findings with actionable remediation at the output path for the audit type.
</objective>

<zone_constraints>
## Zone Constraints

Three-Zone Model per CLAUDE.loa.md: `.claude/` system = never edit (use `.claude/overrides/` or `.loa.config.yaml`); `grimoires/loa/`, `.beads/` state = read/write; this skill's app zone (`src/`, `lib/`, `app/`) = **Read-only**.

Scope: app-zone files less the `.reviewignore` patterns (read it); `.claude/`, `grimoires/`, `.beads/` and `.run/` are excluded unless `--no-reviewignore` is passed.
</zone_constraints>

<integrity_precheck>
<!-- @skill-include: start integrity_precheck | hash:47b71a70 | DO NOT EDIT — generated from .claude/data/skill-includes/integrity_precheck.md -->
## Integrity Pre-Check (MANDATORY)

Before ANY operation, verify System Zone integrity:

1. Check config: read `integrity_enforcement` in `.loa.config.yaml`
2. If `strict` and drift detected -> **HALT** and report
3. If `warn` -> Log warning and proceed with caution
<!-- @skill-include: end integrity_precheck -->
</integrity_precheck>

<factual_grounding>
<!-- @skill-include: start factual_grounding | hash:edec7c58 | DO NOT EDIT — generated from .claude/data/skill-includes/factual_grounding.md -->
## Factual Grounding (MANDATORY)

Before ANY synthesis, planning, or recommendation:

1. **Extract quotes**: Pull word-for-word text from source files
2. **Cite explicitly**: `"[exact quote]" (file.md:L45)`
3. **Flag assumptions**: Prefix ungrounded claims with `[ASSUMPTION]`

**Grounded Example:**
```
The SDD specifies "PostgreSQL 15 with pgvector extension" (sdd.md:L123)
```

**Ungrounded Example:**
```

```
<!-- @skill-include: end factual_grounding -->
</factual_grounding>

<context_discipline>
<!-- @skill-include: start context_discipline | hash:8b81d75a | DO NOT EDIT — generated from .claude/data/skill-includes/context_discipline.md -->
## Context Discipline

Class: `.run/context-class` (`long` default; `standard` via `LOA_CONTEXT_CLASS=standard` or a
≤200K model). `.claude/protocols/tool-result-clearing.md` — long 20K/50K/30K/150K, standard 2K/5K/3K/15K (single /
accumulated / full file / session) → extract ≤10 files, ≤20 words, file:line to NOTES.md; reason
from it. Big files: `notes-guard.sh read --file F --section <H>` / `--index` first. Start: NOTES.md
"Session Continuity"; end / pre-compaction: update it.
<!-- @skill-include: end context_discipline -->
</context_discipline>

<trajectory_logging>
<!-- @skill-include: start trajectory_logging | hash:e809010f | DO NOT EDIT — generated from .claude/data/skill-includes/trajectory_logging.md -->
## Trajectory Logging

Log each significant step to `grimoires/loa/a2a/trajectory/{agent}-{date}.jsonl`:

```json
{"timestamp": "...", "agent": "...", "action": "...", "reasoning": "...", "grounding": {...}}
```
<!-- @skill-include: end trajectory_logging -->
</trajectory_logging>

<grounding_requirements>
Read the actual implementation (never documentation alone) and cross-reference the technical-debt registry if one exists. Every finding cites the CWE/OWASP/CVE it violates with an absolute URL (not just the name) and quotes the vulnerable code inline. Where purpose or trust context (internal vs external) is unclear, state the assumption; say "Unable to assess" for obfuscated or inaccessible code and record scope limits in the report.
</grounding_requirements>

<workflow>
## Phase -1: Scope

Parallelise (`parallel_threshold`) when the scope warrants; the lead decides. A large scope splits per category (`<parallel_execution>`); otherwise run the 5 categories sequentially.

## Phase 0: Prerequisites Check

Sprint audit: `grimoires/loa/a2a/sprint-N/` exists and its `engineer-feedback.md` says "All good"; otherwise STOP: "Sprint must be approved by senior lead before security audit". With `flatline_protocol.code_review.enabled: true`, its `adversarial-review.json` must carry `metadata.model` (the gate's `COMPLETED` check); otherwise STOP: re-run the review's Phase 2.5. Deployment audit: `grimoires/loa/deployment/` exists; read `deployment-report.md` for context if present. Codebase audit: no prerequisites.

## Phase 0.5: Scope Analysis

Run `.claude/scripts/security-audit-scope.sh` before detailed analysis. It categorises the surface into Sources, Sinks, Auth and LLM/AI files.

## Phase 1A: Recon Pass

Catalog untrusted entry points and dangerous sinks without investigating yet (lists, trust levels: `resources/REFERENCE.md` §Sources and Sinks). Track them in a working file, e.g. `grimoires/loa/a2a/audits/YYYY-MM-DD/SECURITY_ANALYSIS_TODO.md`, with file:line, trust level and a status (`PENDING` → `CONFIRMED` / `SAFE` / `PARTIAL` / `N/A`) per item. On a large repo, prioritize by sink severity and reachability; cap entries, log the overflow.

## Phase 1B: Investigate Pass

Trace each flagged source forward to a sink or sanitizer (is the data validated/escaped first?) and each flagged sink backward to every source that reaches it (authorization and input-validation guards?), including second-order flows where stored data becomes dangerous on retrieval. Record each confirmed or dismissed path in the working file. If tracing outruns the time budget, mark the rest deferred, log it, and continue.

## Phase 1C: Security Dissenter Analysis

Runs when `flatline_protocol.security_audit.enabled: true`; skipping it blocks the `COMPLETED` marker write (`adversarial-review-gate.sh`). Emergency override: `LOA_ADVERSARIAL_REVIEW_ENFORCE=false`, noted in sprint notes.

Run `.claude/scripts/adversarial-review.sh --type audit --sprint-id <sprint_id> --diff-range main...HEAD --json` — no `--context-file`. Two voices by default (`companion_voice`). Output: `grimoires/loa/a2a/{sprint_id}/adversarial-audit.json`; one top-level bullet per rejected payload (`rejected_summary` or sidecar rows, whichever is more) under `## Rejected dissent payloads`, else `verdict-derive.sh` fails the trailer. Mechanics: `resources/ADVERSARIAL-REVIEW.md`.
Read `advisory_voices[].findings` as advisory input, never tallied; `metadata.locality.degraded_security_review: true` ⇒ state DEGRADED_SECURITY_REVIEW.

## Phase 1: Systematic Audit

Execute by category (sequential, or split per Phase -1), each per its `resources/REFERENCE.md` section: **Security**, **Architecture**, **Code Quality**, **DevOps**, and **Blockchain/Crypto** when applicable.

## Phase 2: Report Generation

Use `resources/templates/audit-report.md`. Output stays in the State Zone: codebase audits → `grimoires/loa/a2a/audits/YYYY-MM-DD/SECURITY-AUDIT-REPORT.md` plus files under `remediation/` (Write creates it); sprint audits → `grimoires/loa/a2a/sprint-N/auditor-sprint-feedback.md`; deployment audits → `grimoires/loa/a2a/deployment-feedback.md`.

### Coverage

Report every finding you actually observe — minor, uncertain, or on an otherwise clean sprint;
the tally below is the filter, and a finding you drop here is lost.

Each finding carries a `file:line`, a concrete failure scenario, a severity
(`critical|high|medium|low`) and an independent confidence (`high|medium|low`): severity is the
damage if the scenario happens, confidence is how sure you are that it happens. Reserve
`critical` for a confirmed, exploitable path — it can never be excluded from the tally, so a
false positive there is the most expensive mistake in the report.

Every `critical` and `high` is tallied whatever its confidence, except a finding you mark
`speculative` with confidence `low`: list it under `## Observations`, leave it out of the tally,
and record the count in the trailer as `excluded` (a critical is never excludable). `medium` and
`low` are tallied and reported but never force the verdict. You do not decide the verdict; the
counts do.

Confirm the review's demotions independently: for each high the review trailer counts under
`excluded`, either confirm it (still speculative, still low confidence) or tally it as a finding
of your own; record the confirmed count in the trailer as `excluded_confirmed`.

## Phase 2.5: Severity Tally (before the Verdict)

Count every finding from Phase 1 by severity into a literal table — `verdict-derive.sh` checks this against the trailer:

| Severity | Count |
|----------|-------|
| Critical | {N} |
| High | {N} |
| Medium | {N} |
| Low | {N} |

</workflow>

# Audit Sprint

## Purpose

Security and quality audit of sprint implementation as the Paranoid Cypherpunk Auditor. Final gate before sprint completion. Runs AFTER senior lead approval.

## Invocation

```
/audit-sprint sprint-1
/audit-sprint sprint-1 background
```

## Agent

Launches `auditing-security` from `skills/auditing-security/`.

See: `skills/auditing-security/SKILL.md` for full workflow details.

## Prerequisites

- Sprint tasks implemented (`/implement`)
- Senior lead approved with "All good" (`/review-sprint`)
- Not already completed (no COMPLETED marker)

## Workflow

1. **Pre-flight**: Validate sprint ID, verify senior approval
2. **Context Loading**: Read PRD, SDD, sprint plan, implementation report
3. **Code Audit**: Read actual code files for security review
4. **Security Checklist**: OWASP Top 10, secrets, auth, input validation
5. **Decision**: Approve or require changes
6. **Output**: Write audit feedback or approval
7. **Completion**: Create COMPLETED marker on approval
8. **Analytics**: Update usage metrics (THJ users only)

## Arguments

| Argument | Description | Required |
|----------|-------------|----------|
| `sprint_id` | Which sprint to audit (e.g., `sprint-1`) | Yes |
| `background` | Run as subagent for parallel execution | No |

## Outputs

| Path | Description |
|------|-------------|
| `grimoires/loa/a2a/{sprint_id}/auditor-sprint-feedback.md` | Audit results |
| `grimoires/loa/a2a/{sprint_id}/COMPLETED` | Completion marker |
| `grimoires/loa/a2a/index.md` | Updated sprint status |

## Decision Outcomes

### Approval ("APPROVED - LETS FUCKING GO")

When security audit passes:
- Writes approval to `auditor-sprint-feedback.md`
- Creates `COMPLETED` marker file
- Sets sprint status to `COMPLETED`
- Next step: Move to next sprint or deployment

### Changes Required ("CHANGES_REQUIRED")

When security issues found:
- Writes detailed findings to `auditor-sprint-feedback.md`
- Includes severity (CRITICAL/HIGH/MEDIUM/LOW)
- Sets sprint status to `AUDIT_CHANGES_REQUIRED`
- Next step: `/implement sprint-N` (to fix issues)

## Security Checklist

The auditor reviews:
- **Secrets**: No hardcoded credentials, proper env vars
- **Auth/Authz**: Proper access control, no privilege escalation
- **Input Validation**: No injection vulnerabilities
- **Data Privacy**: No PII leaks, proper encryption
- **API Security**: Rate limiting, CORS, validation
- **Error Handling**: No info disclosure, proper logging
- **Code Quality**: No obvious bugs, tested error paths

## Error Handling

| Error | Cause | Resolution |
|-------|-------|------------|
| "Invalid sprint ID" | Wrong format | Use `sprint-N` format |
| "Sprint directory not found" | No A2A dir | Run `/implement` first |
| "No implementation report found" | Missing reviewer.md | Run `/implement` first |
| "Sprint has not been reviewed" | Missing engineer-feedback.md | Run `/review-sprint` first |
| "Sprint has not been approved" | No "All good" | Get senior approval first |
| "Sprint is already COMPLETED" | COMPLETED marker exists | No audit needed |

## Feedback Loop

```
/audit-sprint sprint-N
      ↓
[Security audit]
      ↓
CHANGES_REQUIRED          APPROVED
      ↓                       ↓
/implement sprint-N    [COMPLETED marker]
      ↓                       ↓
/audit-sprint sprint-N   Next sprint
```

## Sprint Ledger Integration

When a Sprint Ledger exists (`grimoires/loa/ledger.json`):

1. **ID Resolution**: Resolves `sprint-1` (local) to global ID (e.g., `3`)
2. **Directory Mapping**: Uses `a2a/sprint-3/` instead of `a2a/sprint-1/`
3. **Status Update**: Sets sprint status to `completed` in ledger on approval
4. **Consistent Paths**: All file operations use resolved global ID

### Example Resolution

```bash
# In cycle-002, sprint-1 maps to global sprint-3
/audit-sprint sprint-1
# → Resolving sprint-1 to global sprint-3
# → Reading: grimoires/loa/a2a/sprint-3/engineer-feedback.md
# → Writing: grimoires/loa/a2a/sprint-3/auditor-sprint-feedback.md
# → Creating: grimoires/loa/a2a/sprint-3/COMPLETED
# → Updating ledger: sprint-3 status = completed
```

### Legacy Mode

Without a ledger, sprint IDs are used directly (sprint-1 → a2a/sprint-1/).

## beads_rust Integration

When beads_rust is installed, the agent records security audit results:

1. **Session Start**: `br sync --import-only` to import latest state
2. **Record Audit**: `br comments add <task-id> "SECURITY AUDIT: [verdict] - [summary]"`
3. **Mark Status**: `br label add <task-id> security-approved` or `security-blocked`
4. **Session End**: `br sync --flush-only` before commit

**Protocol Reference**: See `.claude/protocols/beads-integration.md`

## Phase -1: Scope

Parallelise (`parallel_threshold`) when the scope warrants; the lead decides. A large scope splits per category (`<parallel_execution>`); otherwise run the 5 categories sequentially.

## Phase 0: Prerequisites Check

Sprint audit: `grimoires/loa/a2a/sprint-N/` exists and its `engineer-feedback.md` says "All good"; otherwise STOP: "Sprint must be approved by senior lead before security audit". With `flatline_protocol.code_review.enabled: true`, its `adversarial-review.json` must carry `metadata.model` (the gate's `COMPLETED` check); otherwise STOP: re-run the review's Phase 2.5. Deployment audit: `grimoires/loa/deployment/` exists; read `deployment-report.md` for context if present. Codebase audit: no prerequisites.

## Phase 0.5: Scope Analysis

Run `.claude/scripts/security-audit-scope.sh` before detailed analysis. It categorises the surface into Sources, Sinks, Auth and LLM/AI files.

## Phase 1A: Recon Pass

Catalog untrusted entry points and dangerous sinks without investigating yet (lists, trust levels: `resources/REFERENCE.md` §Sources and Sinks). Track them in a working file, e.g. `grimoires/loa/a2a/audits/YYYY-MM-DD/SECURITY_ANALYSIS_TODO.md`, with file:line, trust level and a status (`PENDING` → `CONFIRMED` / `SAFE` / `PARTIAL` / `N/A`) per item. On a large repo, prioritize by sink severity and reachability; cap entries, log the overflow.

## Phase 1B: Investigate Pass

Trace each flagged source forward to a sink or sanitizer (is the data validated/escaped first?) and each flagged sink backward to every source that reaches it (authorization and input-validation guards?), including second-order flows where stored data becomes dangerous on retrieval. Record each confirmed or dismissed path in the working file. If tracing outruns the time budget, mark the rest deferred, log it, and continue.

## Phase 1C: Security Dissenter Analysis

Runs when `flatline_protocol.security_audit.enabled: true`; skipping it blocks the `COMPLETED` marker write (`adversarial-review-gate.sh`). Emergency override: `LOA_ADVERSARIAL_REVIEW_ENFORCE=false`, noted in sprint notes.

Run `.claude/scripts/adversarial-review.sh --type audit --sprint-id <sprint_id> --diff-range main...HEAD --json` — no `--context-file`. Two voices by default (`companion_voice`). Output: `grimoires/loa/a2a/{sprint_id}/adversarial-audit.json`; one top-level bullet per rejected payload (`rejected_summary` or sidecar rows, whichever is more) under `## Rejected dissent payloads`, else `verdict-derive.sh` fails the trailer. Mechanics: `resources/ADVERSARIAL-REVIEW.md`.
Read `advisory_voices[].findings` as advisory input, never tallied; `metadata.locality.degraded_security_review: true` ⇒ state DEGRADED_SECURITY_REVIEW.

## Phase 1: Systematic Audit

Execute by category (sequential, or split per Phase -1), each per its `resources/REFERENCE.md` section: **Security**, **Architecture**, **Code Quality**, **DevOps**, and **Blockchain/Crypto** when applicable.

## Phase 2: Report Generation

Use `resources/templates/audit-report.md`. Output stays in the State Zone: codebase audits → `grimoires/loa/a2a/audits/YYYY-MM-DD/SECURITY-AUDIT-REPORT.md` plus files under `remediation/` (Write creates it); sprint audits → `grimoires/loa/a2a/sprint-N/auditor-sprint-feedback.md`; deployment audits → `grimoires/loa/a2a/deployment-feedback.md`.

### Coverage

Report every finding you actually observe — minor, uncertain, or on an otherwise clean sprint;
the tally below is the filter, and a finding you drop here is lost.

Each finding carries a `file:line`, a concrete failure scenario, a severity
(`critical|high|medium|low`) and an independent confidence (`high|medium|low`): severity is the
damage if the scenario happens, confidence is how sure you are that it happens. Reserve
`critical` for a confirmed, exploitable path — it can never be excluded from the tally, so a
false positive there is the most expensive mistake in the report.

Every `critical` and `high` is tallied whatever its confidence, except a finding you mark
`speculative` with confidence `low`: list it under `## Observations`, leave it out of the tally,
and record the count in the trailer as `excluded` (a critical is never excludable). `medium` and
`low` are tallied and reported but never force the verdict. You do not decide the verdict; the
counts do.

Confirm the review's demotions independently: for each high the review trailer counts under
`excluded`, either confirm it (still speculative, still low confidence) or tally it as a finding
of your own; record the confirmed count in the trailer as `excluded_confirmed`.

## Phase 2.5: Severity Tally (before the Verdict)

Count every finding from Phase 1 by severity into a literal table — `verdict-derive.sh` checks this against the trailer:

| Severity | Count |
|----------|-------|
| Critical | {N} |
| High | {N} |
| Medium | {N} |
| Low | {N} |

Severity calibration and worked examples: `resources/RUBRICS.md`. These counts drive the verdict below. One-way rule: `critical + high > 0` forces `CHANGES_REQUIRED`; zero critical/high does not itself force `APPROVED` — medium/low accumulation is still your judgment.

## Phase 3: Verdict

**Sprint/Deployment Audit:**
- If ANY CRITICAL or HIGH issues (per Phase 2.5 tally): "CHANGES_REQUIRED"

**Date:** 2026-10-22
**Sprint Reference:** grimoires/loa/sprint.md
**Implementation Report:** grimoires/loa/a2a/sprint-1/reviewer.md (the PR description, `pr/PR.md`)

---

## Overall Assessment

The PR (sprint-252 decision surfaces, part 1) adds the decision-ledger writer `dec-write-lib.sh`, a `--type decisions` validator, the operator-only `/decisions` command and allowlist, the default-off SessionStart surface, the `rounds` interview pacing with its transcript checker, and the grimoire-index `decisions` family. The agents-md-gen count/checksum tests could not be verified (this workspace carries a different command set); `grimoires/loa/decisions.yaml` itself is not in the PR and is assumed to pre-exist tracked, as the tests assume.

The core invariant the PR sells, however, does not hold. The live-run guard on `confirm` is a `cmd | grep -q` pipeline under `set -o pipefail`: with two or more live signals (the normal autonomous shape, a fresh `.run/unattended.json` plus a RUNNING run state) the producer dies of SIGPIPE, the pipeline returns 141, and confirm proceeds. Reproduced 5 of 5 times. A second attribution defect makes the PRD `**Status:**` line, a permanent planning artifact, drive operator-facing operations: an operator confirm records `decided_by: agent`, an operator reject of a decided row is refused, an operator supersede lands as an agent proposal. Further: `--file <live path>` bypasses the CI/hook/worktree refusals; rejecting a proposed replacement leaves a stale `supersede_proposed_by` that blocks every later agent supersede and makes the operator's reject of the original abort; `import` commits the live ledger before rewrites and before removing the pending file, so a partial failure duplicates rows on retry and a concurrent worker's row is dropped; and the validator's merge-base path false-fails any branch where one row moved open → proposed → decided.

Adversarial dissent (two independent voices, gpt-5.5-pro via codex-headless and claude-headless) ran against `pr/head.diff`; its four BLOCKING findings were each verified in a scratch tree before being counted below; its advisory findings are triaged under Cross-Model Observations. No payload was rejected.

**Verdict:** CHANGES REQUIRED

---

## Changes Required

### 1. Security / Integrity — the operator-only guard on `confirm` fails under the normal autonomous-run shape (dissent DISS-C-001, verified)

- **CRITICAL** (confidence: high) `head/.claude/scripts/lib/dec-write-lib.sh:184` — `live_run_signal(){ ctx_signals | grep -q '^live ' ; }` runs under `set -euo pipefail`; `grep -q` exits on the first match, `ctx_signals` then writes its next line into a closed pipe, dies with SIGPIPE (141), and the pipeline is false, so `if live_run_signal; then die …` at `head/.claude/scripts/lib/dec-write-lib.sh:509` never fires when two or more live signals exist.
**File:** `head/.claude/scripts/lib/dec-write-lib.sh:184`, used at `head/.claude/scripts/lib/dec-write-lib.sh:509`
**Issue:** Reproduced in a scratch copy: `context --set-unattended` (fresh marker) plus `.run/sprint-plan-state.json` `{"state":"RUNNING"}` → `context --why` lists two `live` signals → `confirm --id DEC-000N --recorded-by decisions-command --evidence cli:…` succeeded 5/5 times and every row became `decided`. The isolated pipeline (`f | grep -q` with a `jq` fork between echoes) returned 141 on 3/3 runs. `autonomous-agent/SKILL.md:66` now tells every unattended run to write the marker while the run state is RUNNING, which is exactly the two-signal shape.
**Why This Matters:** `decisions.md:59` and the file header (`:17`) promise that confirm refuses during a live unattended run; this is the invariant that keeps agent-proposed rows `proposed` until a human confirms. It silently does not hold.
**Required Fix:** Capture, then test: `live_run_signal(){ local s; s="$(ctx_signals)" || true; grep -q '^live ' <<< "$s"; }` (or test `is_unattended`-style on the captured string). Add a bats case with two live signals (marker + RUNNING) asserting confirm exits 1.
**Reference:** CWE-754 (improper check for unusual or exceptional conditions); bash pipefail + SIGPIPE semantics.

### 2. Functionality / Attribution — the PRD Status line is treated as a live unattended signal for operator operations (verified)

- **HIGH** (confidence: high) `head/.claude/scripts/lib/dec-write-lib.sh:183` — `is_unattended()` is true on any `ctx_signals` line, including `prd prd-status` (`:177-180`), so with `grimoires/loa/prd.md` carrying `**Status:** Draft (autonomous run)` the operator's own calls are demoted: `confirm --answer-ref cli:…` has its ref dropped at `:314` and records `decided_by: agent` (`:538`); `reject` of a decided row dies at `:575`; `supersede` by the operator takes the agent path at `:600-611`.
**File:** `head/.claude/scripts/lib/dec-write-lib.sh:183` (also `:313-317`, `:575`, `:600-611`)
**Issue:** Reproduced: with that PRD line, `confirm --recorded-by decisions-command --evidence cli:… --answer-ref cli:…` → WARN "--answer-ref ignored" and the row reads `decided_by: agent, decided_by_ref: null` while its last transition says `by: operator:decisions-command`; `reject --id DEC-0001 --recorded-by decisions-command` → "the context is unattended; the operator rejects it interactively" (exit 1); operator `supersede` left DEC-0001 `decided` with `supersede_proposed_by` and the new row `proposed_by: agent`. The PRD Status line persists after an autonomous planning run, so these operations stay broken for the whole cycle. The PR's own test at `head/tests/unit/dec-write-lib.bats:355-367` shows the intent (the PRD line must not block confirm) but only asserts `.status`, not `decided_by`.
**Why This Matters:** `decided_by` is the field the whole feature exists to make trustworthy ("which decisions did a human take?"). Here a human confirmation is recorded as the agent's, and the operator cannot reject or supersede.
**Required Fix:** Split the scopes: the PRD line is a planning-time default for `new`/`decide` only (status → proposed, refs ignored); `confirm`, `reject`, `supersede` and `context`'s verdict follow live signals only (`live_run_signal`, once fixed per §1). - **HIGH** (confidence: high) `head/.claude/scripts/lib/dec-write-lib.sh:251` — every `--file` target is `TARGET_KIND="fixture"` and returns before the `ci_blocked` check at `:261`, so `CI=1 dec-write-lib.sh new --file grimoires/loa/decisions.yaml …` writes the live ledger (reproduced: exit 0, row appended), a hook with `LOA_HOOK_CONTEXT=1` can do the same, a linked worktree can write the main ledger by path instead of its pending file, and `confirm`/`supersede` on a `--file …/decisions-pending.yaml` escape their pending-file refusals at `:512` and `:593`.

**Issue:** The header (`:22-23`) promises "Live-ledger writes exit 1 under CI, GITHUB_ACTIONS or LOA_HOOK_CONTEXT=1 (--file fixtures are exempt)"; the exemption is decided by flag presence, not by what the path is.
**Why This Matters:** The CI/hook refusal is the mechanical fence keeping unattended automation out of tracked team state; a path argument should not defeat it.
**Required Fix:** Classify an explicit `--file` by its canonical path (live ledger of this or the main checkout → `live`; `grimoires/loa/a2a/<dir>/decisions-pending.yaml` → `pending`; else `fixture`) and apply the CI/hook and worktree rules to the first two. **Why This Matters:** One rejected proposal permanently freezes a decision for every non-operator voice and blocks the operator's reject, contradicting the lifecycle in the header and `decisions.md`.
**Required Fix:** In `op_reject`, when the rejected row has `.supersedes`, load the predecessor, clear `supersede_proposed_by` if it equals the rejected id, `replace_row` it and add it to the touched list; teach the validator's `supersedes` rule that a `rejected` successor is a legal terminal state. **File:** `head/.claude/scripts/lib/dec-write-lib.sh:647-655`
**Issue:** The failure path is concrete (`chmod a-w` on a rewrite target's directory makes `mktemp` fail); the recovery path produces duplicate decision rows in an append-only ledger that can only be cleaned by rejecting them one by one.
**Why This Matters:** The ledger is tracked team state and the source for the PRD/SDD appendices and the PR body; duplicated rows with diverging references corrupt exactly what the PR sets out to make auditable.
**Required Fix:** Rename or remove the pending file (e.g. to `.imported`) immediately after `verify_and_swap` succeeds and before rewrites; make each rewrite failure warn-and-continue; print the PEND→DEC map before rewrites so a retry can be done by hand. # Sprint 1 Review Feedback

**Reviewer:** Senior Tech Lead Reviewer Agent
**Date:** 2026-10-22
**Sprint Reference:** grimoires/loa/sprint.md
**Implementation Report:** grimoires/loa/a2a/sprint-1/reviewer.md (the PR description, `pr/PR.md`)

---

## Overall Assessment

The PR (sprint-252 decision surfaces, part 1) adds the decision-ledger writer `dec-write-lib.sh`, a `--type decisions` validator, the operator-only `/decisions` command and allowlist, the default-off SessionStart surface, the `rounds` interview pacing with its transcript checker, and the grimoire-index `decisions` family. The code is careful in many places (yq values only through `env()`, rows built by `jq --arg`, verify-before-rename, hostile-string corpus, L6 fencing of the surface), and the PR's own bats suites pass when run here: dec-write-lib 44/44, loa-decisions-surface 8/8, check-round-independence 13/13, user-invoked-commands 12/12, user-invoked-harness 4/4 offline (live test skipped), grimoire-index decisions 5/5, validate-artifact 51/51. The agents-md-gen count/checksum tests could not be verified (this workspace carries a different command set); `grimoires/loa/decisions.yaml` itself is not in the PR and is assumed to pre-exist tracked, as the tests assume.

The core invariant the PR sells, however, does not hold. The live-run guard on `confirm` is a `cmd | grep -q` pipeline under `set -o pipefail`: with two or more live signals (the normal autonomous shape, a fresh `.run/unattended.json` plus a RUNNING run state) the producer dies of SIGPIPE, the pipeline returns 141, and confirm proceeds. Reproduced 5 of 5 times. A second attribution defect makes the PRD `**Status:**` line, a permanent planning artifact, drive operator-facing operations: an operator confirm records `decided_by: agent`, an operator reject of a decided row is refused, an operator supersede lands as an agent proposal. Further: `--file <live path>` bypasses the CI/hook/worktree refusals; rejecting a proposed replacement leaves a stale `supersede_proposed_by` that blocks every later agent supersede and makes the operator's reject of the original abort; `import` commits the live ledger before rewrites and before removing the pending file, so a partial failure duplicates rows on retry and a concurrent worker's row is dropped; and the validator's merge-base path false-fails any branch where one row moved open → proposed → decided.

Adversarial dissent (two independent voices, gpt-5.5-pro via codex-headless and claude-headless) ran against `pr/head.diff`; its four BLOCKING findings were each verified in a scratch tree before being counted below; its advisory findings are triaged under Cross-Model Observations. No payload was rejected.

**Verdict:** CHANGES REQUIRED

---

## Changes Required

### 1. Security / Integrity — the operator-only guard on `confirm` fails under the normal autonomous-run shape (dissent DISS-C-001, verified)

- **CRITICAL** (confidence: high) `head/.claude/scripts/lib/dec-write-lib.sh:184` — `live_run_signal(){ ctx_signals | grep -q '^live ' ; }` runs under `set -euo pipefail`; `grep -q` exits on the first match, `ctx_signals` then writes its next line into a closed pipe, dies with SIGPIPE (141), and the pipeline is false, so `if live_run_signal; then die …` at `head/.claude/scripts/lib/dec-write-lib.sh:509` never fires when two or more live signals exist.
**File:** `head/.claude/scripts/lib/dec-write-lib.sh:184`, used at `head/.claude/scripts/lib/dec-write-lib.sh:509`
**Issue:** Reproduced in a scratch copy: `context --set-unattended` (fresh marker) plus `.run/sprint-plan-state.json` `{"state":"RUNNING"}` → `context --why` lists two `live` signals → `confirm --id DEC-000N --recorded-by decisions-command --evidence cli:…` succeeded 5/5 times and every row became `decided`. The isolated pipeline (`f | grep -q` with a `jq` fork between echoes) returned 141 on 3/3 runs. `autonomous-agent/SKILL.md:66` now tells every unattended run to write the marker while the run state is RUNNING, which is exactly the two-signal shape.
**Why This Matters:** `decisions.md:59` and the file header (`:17`) promise that confirm refuses during a live unattended run; this is the invariant that keeps agent-proposed rows `proposed` until a human confirms. It silently does not hold.
**Required Fix:** Capture, then test: `live_run_signal(){ local s; s="$(ctx_signals)" || true; grep -q '^live ' <<< "$s"; }` (or test `is_unattended`-style on the captured string). Add a bats case with two live signals (marker + RUNNING) asserting confirm exits 1.
**Reference:** CWE-754 (improper check for unusual or exceptional conditions); bash pipefail + SIGPIPE semantics.

### 2. Functionality / Attribution — the PRD Status line is treated as a live unattended signal for operator operations (verified)

- **HIGH** (confidence: high) `head/.claude/scripts/lib/dec-write-lib.sh:183` — `is_unattended()` is true on any `ctx_signals` line, including `prd prd-status` (`:177-180`), so with `grimoires/loa/prd.md` carrying `**Status:** Draft (autonomous run)` the operator's own calls are demoted: `confirm --answer-ref cli:…` has its ref dropped at `:314` and records `decided_by: agent` (`:538`); `reject` of a decided row dies at `:575`; `supersede` by the operator takes the agent path at `:600-611`.
**File:** `head/.claude/scripts/lib/dec-write-lib.sh:183` (also `:313-317`, `:575`, `:600-611`)
**Issue:** Reproduced: with that PRD line, `confirm --recorded-by decisions-command --evidence cli:… --answer-ref cli:…` → WARN "--answer-ref ignored" and the row reads `decided_by: agent, decided_by_ref: null` while its last transition says `by: operator:decisions-command`; `reject --id DEC-0001 --recorded-by decisions-command` → "the context is unattended; the operator rejects it interactively" (exit 1); operator `supersede` left DEC-0001 `decided` with `supersede_proposed_by` and the new row `proposed_by: agent`. The PRD Status line persists after an autonomous planning run, so these operations stay broken for the whole cycle. The PR's own test at `head/tests/unit/dec-write-lib.bats:355-367` shows the intent (the PRD line must not block confirm) but only asserts `.status`, not `decided_by`.
**Why This Matters:** `decided_by` is the field the whole feature exists to make trustworthy ("which decisions did a human take?"). Here a human confirmation is recorded as the agent's, and the operator cannot reject or supersede.
**Required Fix:** Split the scopes: the PRD line is a planning-time default for `new`/`decide` only (status → proposed, refs ignored); `confirm`, `reject`, `supersede` and `context`'s verdict follow live signals only (`live_run_signal`, once fixed per §1). Extend the bats test to assert `decided_by == operator` with the PRD line present.

### 3. Security — `--file <live ledger>` bypasses the CI/hook refusal and the worktree redirect (verified)

- **HIGH** (confidence: high) `head/.claude/scripts/lib/dec-write-lib.sh:251` — every `--file` target is `TARGET_KIND="fixture"` and returns before the `ci_blocked` check at `:261`, so `CI=1 dec-write-lib.sh new --file grimoires/loa/decisions.yaml …` writes the live ledger (reproduced: exit 0, row appended), a hook with `LOA_HOOK_CONTEXT=1` can do the same, a linked worktree can write the main ledger by path instead of its pending file, and `confirm`/`supersede` on a `--file …/decisions-pending.yaml` escape their pending-file refusals at `:512` and `:593`.
**File:** `head/.claude/scripts/lib/dec-write-lib.sh:251`
**Issue:** The header (`:22-23`) promises "Live-ledger writes exit 1 under CI, GITHUB_ACTIONS or LOA_HOOK_CONTEXT=1 (--file fixtures are exempt)"; the exemption is decided by flag presence, not by what the path is.
**Why This Matters:** The CI/hook refusal is the mechanical fence keeping unattended automation out of tracked team state; a path argument should not defeat it.
**Required Fix:** Classify an explicit `--file` by its canonical path (live ledger of this or the main checkout → `live`; `grimoires/loa/a2a/<dir>/decisions-pending.yaml` → `pending`; else `fixture`) and apply the CI/hook and worktree rules to the first two. Add bats cases for `CI=1 … --file grimoires/loa/decisions.yaml` (exit 1) and `confirm --file <pending>` (exit 1).
**Reference:** CWE-284 (improper access control).

### 4. Functionality — rejecting a proposed replacement leaves a stale `supersede_proposed_by` (dissent DISS-003 / DISS-C-005, verified)

- **HIGH** (confidence: high) `head/.claude/scripts/lib/dec-write-lib.sh:580-585` — `op_reject` rewrites only the rejected row; when that row `supersedes` a decided row, the predecessor keeps `supersede_proposed_by: <rejected id>`, so every later agent `supersede` dies at `:601` ("a replacement is already proposed") and the operator's `reject` of the predecessor aborts in `verify_and_swap` because the validator (`head/.claude/scripts/validate-artifact.sh` supersedes rule) sees a row superseding a `rejected` row.
**File:** `head/.claude/scripts/lib/dec-write-lib.sh:580-585` (and `:601`)
**Issue:** Reproduced: agent `supersede` DEC-0001 → DEC-0002; operator `reject` DEC-0002 → DEC-0001 still `supersede_proposed_by: DEC-0002`; agent `supersede` DEC-0001 → exit 1 "already proposed"; operator `reject` DEC-0001 → "ABORT … DEC-0002: supersedes DEC-0001, which is "rejected" and does not name this row".
**Why This Matters:** One rejected proposal permanently freezes a decision for every non-operator voice and blocks the operator's reject, contradicting the lifecycle in the header and `decisions.md`.
**Required Fix:** In `op_reject`, when the rejected row has `.supersedes`, load the predecessor, clear `supersede_proposed_by` if it equals the rejected id, `replace_row` it and add it to the touched list; teach the validator's `supersedes` rule that a `rejected` successor is a legal terminal state. Add a bats case: supersede (agent) → reject → supersede (agent) succeeds; and reject of a decided row with a rejected successor succeeds.

### 5. Data integrity — `import` commits the live ledger before rewrites and before removing the pending file; no idempotency (dissent DISS-002 / DISS-C-004, verified by reading)

- **HIGH** (confidence: medium) `head/.claude/scripts/lib/dec-write-lib.sh:647-655` — `verify_and_swap` lands the imported rows at `:647`, then the `--rewrite` loop runs `mktemp "${p}.XXXXXX"` (`:651`) and `mv -f` under `set -e` with no `|| warn`; a read-only target directory or file aborts the script after the ledger changed and before `rm -f -- "$from"` (`:655`). Re-running `import` appends the same rows again under fresh DEC ids (nothing dedupes against already-imported rows), while files rewritten in the first pass keep the first ids.
**File:** `head/.claude/scripts/lib/dec-write-lib.sh:647-655`
**Issue:** The failure path is concrete (`chmod a-w` on a rewrite target's directory makes `mktemp` fail); the recovery path produces duplicate decision rows in an append-only ledger that can only be cleaned by rejecting them one by one.
**Why This Matters:** The ledger is tracked team state and the source for the PRD/SDD appendices and the PR body; duplicated rows with diverging references corrupt exactly what the PR sets out to make auditable.
**Required Fix:** Rename or remove the pending file (e.g. to `.imported`) immediately after `verify_and_swap` succeeds and before rewrites; make each rewrite failure warn-and-continue; print the PEND→DEC map before rewrites so a retry can be done by hand. Add a bats case with an unwritable rewrite target.

### 6. Data integrity — `import` removes the pending file without holding any lock on it (dissent DISS-001, verified by reading)

- **HIGH** (confidence: medium) `head/.claude/scripts/lib/dec-write-lib.sh:628` — `acquire_lock "$TARGET"` locks the live ledger only; the pending file is read at `:629`, validated, appended to the live ledger (verify + validator, about a second) and then deleted at `:655`. A worktree writer that appends a PEND row to the same pending file during that window succeeds (its lock lives under the worktree's own `.run`, keyed by its path), and `rm -f -- "$from"` deletes that row silently.
**File:** `head/.claude/scripts/lib/dec-write-lib.sh:628-655`
**Issue:** Lock paths are `${PROJECT_ROOT}/.run/.dec-write-<hash>.lock` (`:203-207`), so even locking `$from` from the main checkout would not coordinate with the worktree's writer; the design has no cross-checkout exclusion for the pending file at all.
**Why This Matters:** Parallel subagents in linked worktrees are the documented reason the pending file exists; a lost PEND row leaves a bead `external_ref` pointing at an id that never becomes a DEC.
**Required Fix:** Lock the pending file by a lock keyed on its canonical path under the main checkout's `.run` from both sides (the worktree writer can resolve `MAIN_ROOT`), hold it from the snapshot through removal, and refuse import when the file changed between snapshot and removal (compare a hash). Add a bats case that appends to the pending file between snapshot and removal.

### 7. Validation — the merge-base path of `--type decisions` false-fails legitimate multi-write histories (verified)

- **HIGH** (confidence: high) `head/.claude/scripts/validate-artifact.sh:550-554` — without `--base-file` the validator compares against the copy at `git merge-base origin/main HEAD`, but applies the single-write rules written for the writer's `--base-file` call: `:671` fails on "more than one transition appended in one write" and `:682` compares every field against only the *last* appended transition, so a row that went open → proposed (decision, rationale, alternatives filled) → decided on one branch reports four violations.
**File:** `head/.claude/scripts/validate-artifact.sh:550-554`, rules at `:671` and `:682`
**Issue:** Reproduced in a scratch repo: commit an `open` row, point `origin/main` at it, `decide` then `confirm`, run `validate-artifact.sh --type decisions --file grimoires/loa/decisions.yaml` → exit 1 with "more than one transition appended in one write" and "content edit to alternatives_considered / decision / rationale".
**Why This Matters:** This default path is what `/validate` or CI will run on a branch; a fail-closed validator that rejects the ordinary lifecycle invites hand edits of the ledger, the one thing the design forbids.
**Required Fix:** Pass a `strict` flag when `--base-file` is given (one write, at most one transition) and, for the merge-base path, accept any number of appended transitions each already checked as a legal step, comparing content fields against the set of appended transitions rather than the last one. Add a bats case for the merge-base path with two writes on one row.

---

## Observations

### 1. Security — `--rewrite` targets are not validated

- **MEDIUM** (confidence: high) `head/.claude/scripts/lib/dec-write-lib.sh:649-654` — `import --rewrite <path>` accepts any path: reproduced with a symlink `/tmp/link.txt → /tmp/outside.txt`; the loop replaced the symlink with a regular file outside the project. No `..` check, no project containment, no symlink refusal, unlike `artifact_path` (`:289-305`) which has all three.
**Suggestion:** Reject `..`, require an existing regular non-symlink file whose canonical path is under `PROJECT_ROOT`, as `artifact_path` already does.
**Benefit:** Keeps the one writer that touches arbitrary files inside the tree it owns.

### 2. Security claim — the operator-only gate is a caller-supplied string (dissent DISS-C-002, advisory)

- **MEDIUM** (confidence: high) `head/.claude/scripts/lib/dec-write-lib.sh:359` — `is_operator_call` is `[[ "$(o recorded-by)" == decisions-command ]]`; any session with Bash can run `confirm … --recorded-by decisions-command --answer-ref cli:…` and record `decided_by: operator`. `disable-model-invocation` hides `/decisions` from the Skill tool and the bats grep covers checked-in text only. The header (`:17`) and `decisions.md:24` state it as a hard property.
**Suggestion:** Say plainly in the header, `decisions.md` and the SDD that the gate is an advisory fence (same class as the framework's other accepted fence gaps), or bind confirm to something the model cannot type (a nonce `/decisions` drops under `.run`).
**Benefit:** The provenance claim readers rely on matches what the writer enforces.

### 3. Testing — the unit suite makes a live, paid model call by default

- **MEDIUM** (confidence: high) `head/tests/unit/user-invoked-harness.bats:134-151` — whenever `claude` is on PATH and `LOA_HARNESS_CHECK` is unset, `bats tests/unit` runs `claude -p` for up to 180 s against the operator's account. Developers' machines routinely have the CLI.

**Benefit:** The inventories stay the source of truth the rules reference.

# auditing-security — Security Dissenter (Phase 1C) detail

SKILL.md Phase 1C names the gate, the hook, the override and the invocation. This file carries
the merge rules and the failed-run record.

## Independence

The dissenter receives the diff only — never `--context-file` with your Phase 1A/1B findings —
so it evaluates the code without anchoring on your conclusions.

## Merging dissenter findings into Phase 2

1. CRITICAL/HIGH findings go into the audit report as findings of your own (they may change the
   verdict and must appear in the Phase 2.5 tally).
2. MEDIUM/LOW findings go under a "Cross-Model Security Observations" section.
3. A dissenter finding that duplicates one of yours is marked "Confirmed by cross-model review".

## Failed or unavailable dissenter

Output file: `grimoires/loa/a2a/{sprint_id}/adversarial-audit.json`. The
`adversarial-review-gate.sh` hook checks that this file parses and carries `metadata.type` and `metadata.model` — a `--record-fallback` record names no model, so it never opens the gate: re-run the dissent (or the operator sets `LOA_ADVERSARIAL_REVIEW_ENFORCE=false`, noted in sprint notes). When `adversarial-audit.json` is ABSENT after the script exits — an aborted run leaves none: at start the script moves the previous round's envelope and sidecars aside as `.prev` and never restores them — record the failure with the script itself (a call this skill's allowlist holds; never a hand-written file):

```bash
.claude/scripts/adversarial-review.sh --type audit --sprint-id <sprint_id> --record-fallback failed --reason "<what happened>"
```

before proceeding. Branch on the `status` line the script prints on stdout, never on exit 2 alone (exit 2 with no status line is a usage error, or a standing envelope that stderr names):

- **An envelope stands after a run that took the run lock** — it is the script's own: triage it; never overwrite it.
- **`failed`** (no envelope: the run aborted) — the call above writes `{"findings": [], "metadata": {"status": "failed", "reason": "<what happened>", "rejected_summary": [], "rejected_sidecars": []}}` under the per-(sprint, gate) run lock. It never writes over an envelope that stands (exit 2), unless the run died before its lock with no status on stdout: what stands is then the previous round's — add `--since <the time on the run's "run started" stderr line>` and an envelope older than that goes aside as `.prev`.
- **`refused_concurrent_run`** (another run — a detached or backgrounded one — holds the run lock; nothing recorded, nothing moved; a `--record-fallback` made meanwhile is refused the same way) — wait until the holding run has exited: an envelope that then stands with a `metadata.timestamp` after your refusal is that run's: triage it as this round's dissent only when its `metadata.scope` is what you asked for (the same `diff_range` and `diff_oids` as your refusal's own `metadata.scope` — the commits, not just the ref names — and `run_tag` null: a chunk driver's tagged run reviewed one chunk); otherwise, or when none stands, run again.
- **`workdir_unavailable`, `nothing_to_review`, `budget_exceeded`, `diff_range_failed`** (the range's `git diff` failed — e.g. a base ref a shallow clone lacks; `workdir_unavailable` with `metadata.path` is a previous round's file that could not be moved aside — make the a2a directory writable; written BEFORE the run lock, or with it released; non-zero exit, stdout only; nothing moved aside, so any envelope at the path is the PREVIOUS run's and never this round's evidence) — record it: `--record-fallback <the status> --reason "<its stdout line>" --since <the run started time>` (it never displaces an envelope written after that) moves that envelope and its `adversarial-rejected-audit*.jsonl` sidecars aside as `<name>.prev` (as a run does at start) before it writes, so `verdict-derive.sh` judges this round's record, not the last round's.

A record names what it moved aside (`metadata.displaced`: status, timestamp, findings, rejected); `verdict-derive.sh` warns when that held findings. `verdict-derive.sh` never scans `.prev` files (they are the previous round's evidence, already triaged in that round's feedback) and reports `.prev` files with NO envelope as a `dissent_aborted` violation, which a fallback record clears; `rejected_sidecars: []` does not silence a canonical `adversarial-rejected-audit*.jsonl` beside it — that is this run's own partial work, counted whether listed or not: triage its rows under `## Rejected dissent payloads`.

Then set a `DEGRADED_SECURITY_REVIEW` marker in the audit report. Empty
findings from a run that completed are a normal pass, not a degraded review.

A bare `planned: false` (the block opted out, `companion_voice: false`) is the operator's choice, not a degradation.
Otherwise a completed run is still a degraded audit when its second voice is missing: `companion_voice.status` `failed`
or `fold_failed`, `counted_as` `duplicate_voice` or `sole_voice`, or `planned: false` WITH a `reason` (a companion that
never started: `no_workdir`, `no_route`, `prompt_copy_failed`) — set the `DEGRADED_SECURITY_REVIEW` marker and name the
reason. On a host with no route to the other family at all (`no_route`: no key and no CLI for it) that marker is set on
every audit; `companion_voice: false` on the block is the operator's way to say one voice is the host's shape.

## Two voices and the rejected-payload contract (cycle-126 FR-2)

**Companion voice (D-2.1).** Every dissent plans a second chain from the *other* provider
family — the primary configured on the block decides: any primary outside the Anthropic family (OpenAI,
Google, xAI, unknown) gets the Anthropic chain (`opus` → `claude-headless`), an Anthropic-family primary gets the OpenAI chain
(`gpt-5.5` → `codex-headless`; KF-002 keeps `gpt-5.5-pro` out of the default). Credential *presence* (env → `.env.local` →
`.env`; the value is never read) decides only where the companion chain starts — with no key it
starts at the CLI hop. Both chains walk in parallel; the two completed envelopes are aggregated
(`verdict_quality.voices_succeeded_ids` lists only completed voices). `companion_voice.status` is `succeeded`,
`failed` or `fold_failed`; `verdict_quality.voices_planned` counts the aggregated envelopes — 2 whenever the companion ran,
completed or not (a failed one is listed in `voices_dropped`) — except a failed companion whose id is one of the primary's
succeeded voices: INV-5 lets it feed no envelope, so `voices_planned` stays 1 and `companion_voice` is its only record; a `duplicate_voice` companion contributes none, and a
dropped entry naming the model the companion answered with is removed (INV-5). `companion_voice.counted_as`
(`independent_voice`, `duplicate_voice`, `sole_voice` — the primary never answered) names the outcome, and `planned: false` with a `reason` (`no_workdir`, `no_route`,
`prompt_copy_failed`) is a companion that never started; a bare `planned: false` is the opt-out. The
companion's findings arrive re-numbered `DISS-C-NNN` with a `voice` field; the primary's carry
`voice` too. `metadata.companion_voice` records `{planned, family, family_basis, chain, model,
status: succeeded|failed|fold_failed, failure_class: auth|model_unavailable|quota|timeout|lock_wait|malformed|null,
cost_cents, attempts}`; a companion whose chain fails is a dropped voice (degraded for an audit,
never blocking a review). Opt-out per block: `flatline_protocol.{code_review,security_audit}.companion_voice: false`
(the YAML boolean spellings in any case; a value that is none of them is reported and the voice stays on).

**Tolerant schema (D-2.2).** A finding missing only `failure_mode` is no longer dropped: the
first sentence of its `description` (≤ 200 chars) becomes `failure_mode` and the finding is
marked `failure_mode_derived: true` (a missing `id` is filled positionally, `id_derived: true`).
Severity, category and description are never touched. Payloads that still fail go to the
sidecar (`adversarial-rejected-<type>.jsonl`, `-companion` suffix for the second voice) **and**
to `metadata.rejected_summary[]` as `{index, severity, title, title_derived, anchor, reason, description_head}`.

**The contract (D-2.3).** When `rejected_summary` is non-empty the feedback file MUST contain a
`## Rejected dissent payloads` section with one line per entry — `- <title> (<severity>, <anchor>)
— <reason>: triaged as <real defect → counted under the matching heading | not a defect → why>`.
`verdict-derive.sh` reads the sibling envelope (`adversarial-<gate>.json`, or `--envelope <path>`)
and marks the trailer INCONSISTENT (exit 1) when the section is missing. Reading a sidecar row:
`payload` is the model's finding as normalised, `reject_reason` the clause it failed, and
`repair_attempted` / `repair_succeeded` whether the bounded repair round-trip ran.

**Round-1 hardening (sprint-248 review, sixteen live two-voice runs).** One list, by envelope field; both skills' copies of
this block are kept byte-identical (CMP-138 fails on any drift).

- **Two voices, one envelope.** The companion runs in its own sub-workdir with a log and its own copies of the prompt files.
  The envelope's `cost_usd` / tokens are BOTH voices; the per-voice spend stays under `companion_voice.cost_cents`, and

SKILL.md Phase 1C names the gate, the hook, the override and the invocation. This file carries
the merge rules and the failed-run record.

## Independence

The dissenter receives the diff only — never `--context-file` with your Phase 1A/1B findings —
so it evaluates the code without anchoring on your conclusions.

## Merging dissenter findings into Phase 2

1. CRITICAL/HIGH findings go into the audit report as findings of your own (they may change the
   verdict and must appear in the Phase 2.5 tally).
2. MEDIUM/LOW findings go under a "Cross-Model Security Observations" section.
3. A dissenter finding that duplicates one of yours is marked "Confirmed by cross-model review".

Output file: `grimoires/loa/a2a/{sprint_id}/adversarial-audit.json`. The
`adversarial-review-gate.sh` hook checks that this file parses and carries `metadata.type` and `metadata.model` — a `--record-fallback` record names no model, so it never opens the gate: re-run the dissent (or the operator sets `LOA_ADVERSARIAL_REVIEW_ENFORCE=false`, noted in sprint notes). When `adversarial-audit.json` is ABSENT after the script exits — an aborted run leaves none: at start the script moves the previous round's envelope and sidecars aside as `.prev` and never restores them — record the failure with the script itself (a call this skill's allowlist holds; never a hand-written file):

```bash
.claude/scripts/adversarial-review.sh --type audit --sprint-id <sprint_id> --record-fallback failed --reason "<what happened>"
```

before proceeding. Branch on the `status` line the script prints on stdout, never on exit 2 alone (exit 2 with no status line is a usage error, or a standing envelope that stderr names):

- **An envelope stands after a run that took the run lock** — it is the script's own: triage it; never overwrite it.
- **`failed`** (no envelope: the run aborted) — the call above writes `{"findings": [], "metadata": {"status": "failed", "reason": "<what happened>", "rejected_summary": [], "rejected_sidecars": []}}` under the per-(sprint, gate) run lock. It never writes over an envelope that stands (exit 2), unless the run died before its lock with no status on stdout: what stands is then the previous round's — add `--since <the time on the run's "run started" stderr line>` and an envelope older than that goes aside as `.prev`.
- **`refused_concurrent_run`** (another run — a detached or backgrounded one — holds the run lock; nothing recorded, nothing moved; a `--record-fallback` made meanwhile is refused the same way) — wait until the holding run has exited: an envelope that then stands with a `metadata.timestamp` after your refusal is that run's: triage it as this round's dissent only when its `metadata.scope` is what you asked for (the same `diff_range` and `diff_oids` as your refusal's own `metadata.scope` — the commits, not just the ref names — and `run_tag` null: a chunk driver's tagged run reviewed one chunk); otherwise, or when none stands, run again.
- **`workdir_unavailable`, `nothing_to_review`, `budget_exceeded`, `diff_range_failed`** (the range's `git diff` failed — e.g. a base ref a shallow clone lacks; `workdir_unavailable` with `metadata.path` is a previous round's file that could not be moved aside — make the a2a directory writable; written BEFORE the run lock, or with it released; non-zero exit, stdout only; nothing moved aside, so any envelope at the path is the PREVIOUS run's and never this round's evidence) — record it: `--record-fallback <the status> --reason "<its stdout line>" --since <the run started time>` (it never displaces an envelope written after that) moves that envelope and its `adversarial-rejected-audit*.jsonl` sidecars aside as `<name>.prev` (as a run does at start) before it writes, so `verdict-derive.sh` judges this round's record, not the last round's.

A record names what it moved aside (`metadata.displaced`: status, timestamp, findings, rejected); `verdict-derive.sh` warns when that held findings. `verdict-derive.sh` never scans `.prev` files (they are the previous round's evidence, already triaged in that round's feedback) and reports `.prev` files with NO envelope as a `dissent_aborted` violation, which a fallback record clears; `rejected_sidecars: []` does not silence a canonical `adversarial-rejected-audit*.jsonl` beside it — that is this run's own partial work, counted whether listed or not: triage its rows under `## Rejected dissent payloads`.

Then set a `DEGRADED_SECURITY_REVIEW` marker in the audit report. Empty
findings from a run that completed are a normal pass, not a degraded review.

A bare `planned: false` (the block opted out, `companion_voice: false`) is the operator's choice, not a degradation.

   390	  ROW="$1" ROWID="$id" yq -i "(.decisions[] | select(.id == strenv(ROWID))) = env(ROW) | ${STYLE_ROW}" "$TMPF" || die "yq update failed; ledger untouched"

   392	# verify_and_swap OLD_JSON ADDED TOUCHED_IDS_JSON
   393	verify_and_swap(){
   394	  local old="$1" added="$2" touched="$3" errs
   395	  # Whole-ledger JSON goes through files (--slurpfile): a large ledger overflows one argv string.
   396	  SCRATCH="$(mktemp "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/dec-verify.XXXXXX")"
   397	  printf '%s' "$old" > "${SCRATCH}.old"
   398	  yq -o=json -I0 '.' "$TMPF" > "${SCRATCH}.new" 2>/dev/null || die "ABORT: the candidate ledger does not parse; ledger untouched"
   399	  errs="$(jq -rn --slurpfile O "${SCRATCH}.old" --slurpfile N "${SCRATCH}.new" --argjson added "$added" --argjson t "$touched" '
   400	    $O[0] as $o | $N[0] as $n
   401	    | ($o.decisions | map(.id)) as $oi | (($n.decisions // []) | map(.id)) as $ni
   402	    | (($n.decisions // []) | map(select(type == "object" and (.id | type) == "string") | {key: .id, value: .}) | from_entries) as $nb
   403	    | ($oi | map({key: ., value: true}) | from_entries) as $os | ($t | map({key: ., value: true}) | from_entries) as $ts
   404	    | [ (if $n.schema_version != 1 then "unknown schema_version" else empty end),
   405	        (if ($n.decisions | type) != "array" then "decisions is not a sequence" else empty end),
   406	        ($oi - $ni | .[] | "would drop id \(.)"),
   407	        ($ni | group_by(.) | map(select(length > 1) | .[0]) | .[] | "duplicate id \(.)"),
   408	        (if ($ni | length) != (($o.decisions | length) + $added) then "row count \($ni | length) != \($o.decisions | length) + \($added)" else empty end),
   409	        ($o.decisions[] as $r | select($ts[$r.id] | not) | select($nb[$r.id] != $r) | "row \($r.id) changed outside this operation"),
   410	        ($n.decisions[] | .id as $x | select($os[$x] | not) | select($ts[$x] | not) | "unexpected new row \($x)")
   411	      ] | .[]')" || die "ABORT: verification failed to run; ledger untouched"
   412	  [[ -z "$errs" ]] || die "ABORT: ${errs//$'\n'/; }; ledger untouched"
   413	  [[ -f "$VALIDATOR" ]] || die "ABORT: validator missing at ${VALIDATOR}; ledger untouched"
   414	  local vout
   415	  if ! vout="$(PROJECT_ROOT="$PROJECT_ROOT" bash "$VALIDATOR" --type decisions --file "$TMPF" --base-file "$TARGET" 2>&1)"; then
   416	    die "ABORT: the candidate fails validate-artifact.sh --type decisions; ledger untouched:"$'\n'"$vout"
   417	  fi
   418	  chmod 0644 "$TMPF"
   419	  mv -f "$TMPF" "$TARGET"; TMPF=""
   420	}

   424	# Build a new row JSON. Args: id status voice ref sha supersedes
   425	build_row(){
   426	  local id="$1" status="$2" voice="$3" ref="$4" sha="$5" sup="$6"
   427	  local summary phase category source decision rationale alts cons rb cyc now ev
   428	  summary="$(san1 "$(o summary)")"; phase="$(san1 "$(o phase)")"; category="$(san1 "$(o category)")"; source="$(san1 "$(o source)")"
   429	  [[ -n "$summary" ]] || usage "--summary is required"
   430	  # characters, not bytes (LC_ALL=C makes ${#x} a byte count): the validator's limit is 160 code points
   431	  [[ "$(jq -rn --arg s "$summary" '$s | length')" -le 160 ]] || die "--summary is over 160 characters; one plain line"
   432	  [[ "$phase" =~ ^(discovery|architecture|sprint-planning|implementation|review|charting|spike|operations)$ ]] || usage "--phase must be discovery|architecture|sprint-planning|implementation|review|charting|spike|operations"
   433	  [[ "$category" =~ ^[a-z][a-z0-9-]*$ ]] || usage "--category must match [a-z][a-z0-9-]* (e.g. scope, technology, architecture)"
   434	  [[ -n "$source" ]] || usage "--source is required (bead id, PR, NOTES anchor, spike path, with a line or anchor)"
   435	  decision="$(san1 "$(o decision)")"; rationale="$(san1 "$(o rationale)")"; alts="$(alts_json)"; cons="$(cons_json)"
   436	  if [[ "$status" == "proposed" ]]; then
   437	    [[ -n "$decision" && -n "$rationale" && "$(printf '%s' "$alts" | jq 'length')" -ge 1 ]] \
   438	      || die "a proposed row needs --decision, --rationale and at least one --alternative-json"
   439	  fi
   440	  rb="$(recorded_by)"; cyc="$(san1 "$(o cycle)")"; [[ -n "$cyc" ]] || cyc="$(default_cycle)"
   441	  if [[ -z "$cyc" ]] && is_unattended; then warn "no cycle id (pass --cycle); the row's cycle is null"; fi
   442	  now="$(now_utc)"; ev="$(san1 "$(o evidence)")"; [[ -n "$ev" ]] || ev="$source"
   443	  jq -cn --arg id "$id" --arg now "$now" --arg phase "$phase" --arg category "$category" --arg summary "$summary" \
   444	    --arg decision "$decision" --arg rationale "$rationale" --argjson alts "$alts" --argjson cons "$cons" \
   445	    --arg voice "$voice" --arg ref "$ref" --arg sha "$sha" --arg rb "${rb}/$(session_id)" --arg by "${voice}:${rb}" \
   446	    --arg commit "$(head_commit)" --arg source "$source" --arg cycle "$cyc" --arg sup "$sup" --arg status "$status" --arg ev "$ev" '
   447	    def n: if . == "" then null else . end;
   448	    {id: $id, created_at: $now, updated_at: $now, phase: $phase, category: $category, summary: $summary,
   449	     decision: ($decision | n), rationale: ($rationale | n),
   450	     alternatives_considered: (if ($alts | length) == 0 then null else $alts end), consequences: $cons,
   451	     proposed_by: $voice, decided_by: null, decided_by_ref: ($ref | n), evidence_sha256: ($sha | n),
   452	     recorded_by: $rb, commit: $commit, source: $source, cycle: ($cycle | n), supersedes: ($sup | n),
   453	     supersede_proposed_by: null, status: $status,
   454	     transitions: [{at: $now, from: null, to: $status, by: $by, evidence: $ev}],
   455	     rejection_rationale: null, follow_up: null, prior_requests: []}'
   456	}

   495	      --arg now "$now" --arg by "$(printf '%s' "$r" | jq -r '.proposed_by'):${rb}" --arg ev "$(san1 "$(o evidence)")" '
